subject.title: All LLM API calls time out simultaneously despite APIs being reachable (multi-agent concurrency issue)

question: Should #43374 remain the canonical live-repro item for multi-agent Telegram/provider timeout investigation, and which owner boundary should be tried first after proof?
rationale: The report crosses Telegram runner concurrency, provider transport, model fallback, session locks, and launch defaults; source confirms partial mitigations and a remaining Telegram concurrency coupling, but not enough to choose a safe product/default change automatically.

options.title: Require current-main live trace first
options.body: Keep the issue open and require a current-main four-agent Telegram run with gateway/provider timing evidence before selecting a code or config change.

options.title: Promote Telegram concurrency decoupling
options.body: Treat the remaining tested maxConcurrent-to-sink coupling as the first repair target, accepting that provider/runtime bottlenecks may remain afterward.

options.title: Close only after mitigation proof
options.body: Consider the merged fallback fixes sufficient only if a current-main reproduction attempt shows the original simultaneous timeout pattern no longer occurs.

recommendation.title: Require current-main live trace first
recommendation.body: Keep the issue open and require a current-main four-agent Telegram run with gateway/provider timing evidence before selecting a code or config change.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is the best available routing owner because current blame and the issue timeline point to this handle across the Telegram, fallback, and provider-runtime decision surfaces.
